company.name: Cactus
company.shortDescription: Cactus offers AI-driven tools to handle admin tasks, qualify leads, manage schedules, answer calls, and engage clients.
company.description: Cactus provides an AI-powered business assistant designed to manage administrative tasks and streamline operations. The platform qualifies new leads based on predefined criteria, follows up automatically, and ensures timely engagement with potential clients. It offers a personalized, fully branded website without coding requirements, enabling businesses to maintain a distinct online presence. It also handles scheduling and coordination, managing calendars, sending reminders, and overseeing daily tasks to maintain smooth operations. Its AI conducts natural, context-aware conversations, scoring leads, and detecting spam while responding instantly to calls and messages. The system operates continuously, allowing businesses to remain responsive and connected regardless of location. IT adapts to various industries, including salons, real estate, and service-based businesses, providing tailored communication and support.

insights.title: Funding is concentrated in the latest major round
insights.statement: The latest disclosed Seed round raised $7,000,000, or 93.33% of reported total funding.
insights.implication: This round accounts for most reported historical financing, making it important when assessing funding-source concentration and fundraising cadence.

insights.title: Valuation increased across disclosed rounds
insights.statement: Known post-money valuation rose from $6,823,975 to $28,214,765, a 4.13x increase.
insights.implication: The disclosed financing history indicates a material valuation step-up between the earliest and latest rounds with known valuations.
caveats: Only rounds with a disclosed post-money valuation are compared.

insights.title: Sharp recent attention and growth momentum
insights.statement: Crunchbase scores growth at 77 (-2 over 90 days) and market heat at 59 (-7).
insights.implication: The company has recently become much more visible, but the scores should be treated as attention/activity indicators rather than revenue or clinical-performance metrics.
